text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — thinking about surfacing SLO thresholds in the console alongside sampling and routing metadata. Current problem: customers see alert floods even when notify sampling applied downstream. We should clarify sampling as part of SLO eval. cc @Maya Patel @Sam Ortiz
Maya Patel: Agree. main UX question: do we surface the effective (post-sampling) alert rate or the raw signal? Users expect to see what they get paged on.
Sam Ortiz: I'd vote effective. We have customers confused by "SLO breaching" counters that don't map to pager ops.
Jordan Lee: How does this interact with routing policies + quotas? If we sample before routing, alarms might still hit tenant quotas.
Alex Chen: That's the trick. Proposal: introduce a "sampling proxy" in API surface that returns both raw_count and effective_count and the routing path used. Example payload:
```
{ "slo_id": "svc.latency_p95",
  "window": "5m",
  "raw_count": 412,
  "effective_count": 32,
  "sampling_policy": "weighted-tenant-0.02",
  "route": "dedicated-west-1" }
```
Maya Patel: +1 for both counts. Also need telemetry contract versioning. If frontend relies on fields, breaking changes are bad.
Kim Brooks: We'll need to add telemetry labels so dashboards can group by sampling_policy and route. Otherwise it's impossible to debug noise sources.
Priya Nair: Ops concern: if effective_count is low due to sampling but raw_count is high, customers might think alerting suppressed incorrectly. We should show a "why suppressed" tooltip.
Sam Ortiz: UX note: show "estimated un-suppressed vs suppressed alerts" and link to runbook. Keep it compact in the SLO card.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: sampling-proxy v0.1 -> staging at 2025-06-02T04:00Z
Jordan Lee: API rules: we need a server-side opt-in flag per-tenant: sampling_preview=true for when we compute effective_count in console. Default false to avoid metrics churn.
Alex Chen: Thinking about quota interplay: if route is 'cheap' vs 'expensive' model tiers, we should expose fallback route history too.
Kim Brooks: On telemetry retention: store raw_count for 90d but effective_count for 365d? Thoughts?
Maya Patel: retention fine but we must document cost impact. storing raw counts for all tenants is expensive.
Priya Nair: As a stopgap, add "preview window" at most 12h for raw breakdowns unless customer enables longer retention.
Sam Ortiz: Implementation note: backend will need to emit an "evaluation_trace_id" so frontend can fetch full trace logs for a given breach event. That helps postmortems.
Alex Chen: Action items: 1) Maya to write telemetry contract doc draft 2) Sam & Jordan to prototype sampling-proxy response in sandbox 3) Kim to spec dashboard changes 4) Priya to draft runbook tooltip copy
Maya Patel: I'll start the doc today. Will post PR link.
Sam Ortiz: I'll spike the sandbox this afternoon, ping if you want to pair.
Jordan Lee: Spinning up a dev branch: feature/sampling-proxy
Kim Brooks: Will sketch a compact UI mock — want to avoid bloating SLO cards.
Priya Nair: Runbook copy: I'll add "why suppressed" + "how to disable sampling for critical tenants".
Alex Chen: Thanks team. If we can get an internal API contract by EOW we can start a canary roll.
Maya Patel: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/telemetry/compare/sampling-proxy
infra-bot: Canary deploy started: sampling-proxy v0.1 -> canary cluster
Sam Ortiz: Seeing test payloads look reasonable, posting logs in the sandbox channel.
Jordan Lee: Reminder: ensure last_message_ts updated when we merge.
